corpus_contract.source: the same first four 256-shot chunks from each strict X/Z run used by the frozen decoder latency matrix

external_basis.notes: the sources motivate O(d) overlapping windows, explicit throughput/latency separation, and a roughly 1 microsecond per round target; none validates this host/socket implementation as hardware

hard_boundaries.reason: the transport is a synchronous same-host socketpair and no real QPU, measurement electronics, controller, asynchronous queue, cryogenic link, or device feedback path is present

known_before_preregistration.disclosure: the exact 1,024-shot X/Z corpora and their offline full-block predictions are already public; no overlapping-window prediction, residual, socket-path latency, p99, or deadline-miss outcome has been observed

next_gate: If the online host proxy fails, localize semantic versus tail failure before changing one frozen axis. If it passes, move to a real asynchronous device/control path and model-mismatch stress; hardware, full B2, #023, and B7 remain open either way.

online_software_proxy.interpretation: host-local online software proxy only; it is stricter than the earlier offline median backlog proxy but cannot satisfy a hardware deadline
online_software_proxy.pass_rule: both X and Z require exact equality to all frozen full-block predictions, zero committed/final residual syndrome, nearest-rank p99 end-to-end time <=1 microsecond per committed layer, and deadline miss fraction <=1 percent

question: Can the accepted 71-qubit correlation-aware memory decoder preserve its frozen predictions and a 1 microsecond per syndrome-layer tail budget when converted from offline full-block decoding into sequential O(d) overlapping recovery with a measured host communication and feedback path?

scope.excluded_work: all catalog problems and research tracks other than #021/B7, #022/B2, and #023

timing_contract.primary_statistic: nearest-rank p99 of end-to-end microseconds per committed detector layer
reported_statistics: input, decode/commit, and feedback phase summaries
timing_contract.timing_replay_policy: wall-clock values are non-deterministic; raw timing bytes, arithmetic, structure, corpus, predictions, and verdict logic must be independently auditable

included: detector bit packing and header construction
kernel socket send and receive in both directions
detector bit unpacking and header validation
logical-frame feedback packing, transport, and acknowledgement
transport_contract.input_packet: 16-byte network-order header plus little-endian packed detector bits
transport_contract.model: same-process Unix domain socketpair control-path emulator
transport_contract.prebuffer: the first window_size-stride layers are transported before steady-state timing
transport_contract.timed_end: after the logical-frame feedback acknowledgement is received and verified
transport_contract.timed_start: immediately before packing the newly arrived detector layers for a window

window_contract.algorithm: sequential overlapping recovery with tentative buffer corrections and committed correction propagation
window_contract.commit_rule: commit only correction components triggered by detectors in the oldest stride layers; propagate every committed component endpoint and logical-frame flip into later windows
window_contract.correlation_preservation: Stim suggested graphlike decomposition components remain grouped by their original error instruction inside each window; two-pass PyMatching reweights those components before the commit decision
window_contract.last_window_rule: the final window consumes every remaining detector layer and commits all of them; its size is at most window_size+stride-1
semantic_invariants: every committed detector has zero residual syndrome after its window
the final residual syndrome is zero
all detector input packets reproduce the frozen syndrome exactly
the primary correlated online prediction equals the frozen correlated full-block prediction on every one of 1024 shots per basis
